flashcards.back: The molecule that stores genetic instructions as a sequence of bases, organised into genes on chromosomes.
A length of DNA that codes for one polypeptide chain.
One of the alternative forms of a gene, found at the same locus on homologous chromosomes.
The alleles an organism carries for a gene, such as AA, Aa or aa.
The observable trait an organism shows, produced by its genotype and environment.
An allele that shows in the phenotype whenever it is present, even in a heterozygote.
An allele that shows in the phenotype only when no dominant allele is present.
A change in the DNA base sequence; most mutations are neutral, some are harmful, and a rare few are beneficial.

Mutation sounds like damage. Most mutations are neutral: only some are harmful, and a rare few are the raw material of evolution. In the animation a mutated gene still builds a working protein with the same job: the sequence changed, but nothing that matters did - which is why the blanket claim fails.

items.answer: DNA is transcribed into mRNA in the nucleus, and the mRNA is translated into a polypeptide at a ribosome in the cytoplasm.
items.prompt: Outline the central dogma in one or two sentences, naming where transcription and translation happen.

items.answer: A son has only one X chromosome, so the recessive h allele has no second allele to mask it and the trait shows; a daughter has a second X carrying H, which masks h, so she is a carrier without symptoms.
items.prompt: A carrier mother (X^H X^h) and a normal father (X^H Y) have children. Explain why a son who inherits X^h has haemophilia, while a daughter who inherits X^h usually does not.
